purpose: Sense-level corrections for a third group of existing English baseline entries with multiple parts of speech.
status: editorially-authored; awaiting final review and integration

senses.definition: A choice or possibility that can be used instead of another one.
senses.definitionZh: 替代方案；可供选择的事物
examples: We need an alternative to this expensive tool.
Is there a cheaper alternative?

senses.definition: Different from the usual or existing option and available to be used instead.
examples: Is there an alternative route?
The school offers alternative ways to complete the project.

senses.definition: One or the other of two people or things.
senses.definitionZh: （两者中的）任何一个；或者一个
examples: You can choose either colour.
Either answer is acceptable.

senses.definition: One of two people or things, when the choice is understood from the context.
examples: Either of them would be suitable.
I do not like these shoes; do you have either in a larger size?

senses.definition: Used after a negative statement to mean “also not”.
examples: I do not know the answer either.
She did not call, and he did not write either.

senses.definition: As much or as many as is needed or wanted.
examples: We have enough chairs for everyone.
There is not enough time to finish the test.

senses.definition: The amount or number that is needed or wanted.
examples: I have had enough, thank you.
Enough has been said about the problem.

senses.definition: To the degree or amount that is needed.
examples: The room is warm enough now.
She did not speak loudly enough for everyone to hear.

senses.definition: In a different way or in other circumstances.
senses.definitionZh: 以其他方式；在其他方面
examples: The instructions were clear, but the screen looked otherwise.
You should leave now; otherwise, you may miss the train.

senses.definition: Used to introduce what will happen if something is not done or is not true.
examples: Wear a coat, otherwise you will feel cold.
We must hurry; otherwise, the shop will close.

senses.definition: Able to wait or deal with difficulties without becoming annoyed or upset.
examples: Please be patient while the file uploads.
She is patient when teaching beginners.

senses.definition: A person who receives medical care or treatment.
examples: The doctor spoke with each patient.
The hospital has a separate waiting area for young patients.

senses.definition: Relating to a job or career that requires specialised knowledge or training; or showing the standards expected at work.
senses.definitionZh: 职业的；专业的；符合职业标准的
examples: She wants to build a professional career in design.
Please use a professional tone in the report.

senses.definition: A person who has specialised training or earns a living from a particular activity.
examples: A professional checked the electrical wiring.
He is a professional photographer.

senses.definition: A regular way of doing things, especially as part of everyday life or work.
examples: A short morning routine helps me focus.
The team follows a routine before every performance.

senses.definition: Done regularly as part of a normal process, rather than because something unusual has happened.
examples: The doctor arranged a routine check-up.
The update is part of routine maintenance.

senses.definition: Help, encouragement or practical assistance given to someone or something.
examples: Thank you for your support during the project.
The students receive extra support with reading.

senses.definition: To help, encourage or provide what someone or something needs; or to hold something up.
examples: The evidence supports the main conclusion.
Strong pillars support the roof.

senses.definition: The latest information about a situation, or a newer version of a product or system.
senses.definitionZh: 最新消息；更新；升级版本
examples: The manager gave us an update on the project.
The latest software update fixes several problems.

senses.definition: To make information or a system more current by adding new details or improvements.
examples: Please update your contact details.
The team updated the website this morning.

senses.definition: Unhappy, worried or emotionally disturbed because something unpleasant has happened.
examples: She was upset about the cancellation.
He looked upset after the meeting.

senses.definition: To make someone unhappy or worried, or to disturb a plan or situation.
examples: I did not mean to upset you.
The sudden rain upset our plans for the picnic.

senses.definition: Normal or happening most of the time; expected in a particular situation.
examples: She arrived at her usual time.
The shop was quieter than usual today.

senses.definition: The thing or way that is normally chosen or expected.
senses.definitionZh: 平常的事物；惯常的选择
examples: I'll have my usual, please.
The café was serving the usual for breakfast.

senses.definition: The importance, usefulness or quality of something; or the amount of money something is worth.
examples: The course offers good value for money.
The value of the painting increased over time.

senses.definition: To consider something important or useful, or to estimate how much it is worth.
examples: We value clear communication in our team.
The expert valued the old watch before it was sold.

senses.definition: A raised movement of water; a moving pattern or sudden increase; or a hand movement used as a greeting.
examples: A large wave hit the side of the boat.
She gave us a friendly wave from the doorway.

senses.definition: To move your hand or an object from side to side, often to greet someone or attract attention.
examples: He waved goodbye as the train left.
The guide waved a flag to signal the group.

senses.definition: To speak very quietly, using the breath rather than a normal voice.
examples: Please do not whisper during the presentation.
She whispered the answer to her friend.

senses.definition: A very quiet way of speaking or a quiet sound.
examples: I heard a whisper from the next room.
The room fell to a whisper as the speaker entered.

senses.definition: To think about something with curiosity or uncertainty, wanting to know the answer.
examples: I wonder why the train is late.
She wondered whether she had chosen the right course.

senses.definition: A feeling of surprise and admiration caused by something beautiful or extraordinary; or something remarkable.
examples: The children stared at the fireworks in wonder.
The ancient bridge is an engineering wonder.

senses.definition: Having a particular value or being deserving of the time, effort or attention needed.
examples: The museum is worth visiting.
This old camera is worth a lot of money.

senses.definition: The value or importance of someone or something.
examples: The company estimated the total worth of its equipment.
She knows her own worth and stands by her decisions.

senses.definition: Until now or until a particular time, often used in questions and negative statements.
examples: Have you finished the report yet?
The new timetable has not been announced yet.

senses.definition: But or nevertheless; used to introduce a contrast.
examples: The task was difficult, yet everyone completed it.
He was tired, yet he continued working.

senses.definition: To produce or provide a result, amount or supply; or to give way or stop resisting.
examples: The new method yielded better results.
Drivers must yield to pedestrians at the crossing.

senses.definition: The amount of something produced, especially by a plant, farm, investment or process.
examples: The farm expects a larger rice yield this year.
The investment offers a steady annual yield.

senses.definition: To reply quickly and sharply, often in an angry, witty or challenging way.
examples: “That is not what I said,” she retorted.
He retorted that the figures were incorrect.

senses.definition: A quick, sharp or witty reply.
examples: Her clever retort made the audience laugh.
He had no retort ready when the question was asked.

senses.definition: To move back or away from a difficult, threatening or uncomfortable situation.
examples: The soldiers retreated to a safer position.
He retreated from the argument before it became worse.

senses.definition: An act of moving away from danger or difficulty; or a quiet place or period used for rest and reflection.
examples: The army began its retreat before dawn.
She spent the weekend at a quiet writing retreat.

senses.definition: To move back suddenly because of fear, shock, pain or disgust.
examples: He recoiled when he touched the hot surface.
She recoiled from the unpleasant smell.

senses.definition: A sudden backward movement, especially caused by a force or strong reaction.
examples: The recoil of the tool surprised the new user.
He showed no recoil from the difficult question.

senses.definition: A period or measure of isolation used to prevent the spread of disease or to contain a security threat.
examples: The animal was kept in quarantine before joining the group.
The health authority shortened the quarantine period.

senses.definition: To isolate a person, animal, object or computer system to prevent a risk from spreading.
examples: The clinic quarantined the animal for observation.
The security software quarantined the suspicious file.

senses.definition: To speak about or react to something with contempt or disbelief.
examples: Some people scoffed at the idea before it was tested.
He scoffed when he heard the unlikely story.

senses.definition: Food, especially in informal British and Australian usage.
senses.definitionZh: 食物；吃的东西（非正式用法）
examples: The hikers packed enough scoff for the journey.
After the match, the team sat down for some hot scoff.

senses.definition: To make a very high, loud sound because of fear, excitement or pain.
examples: The children shrieked with excitement on the ride.
She shrieked when the spider appeared.

senses.definition: A very high and loud cry or sound.
examples: A sudden shriek came from the garden.
The machine ended with a loud metallic shriek.

senses.definition: To raise and lower your shoulders to show uncertainty, indifference or that you do not know.
examples: He shrugged when I asked who had moved the chair.
She shrugged her shoulders and continued working.

senses.definition: A movement in which the shoulders are raised and lowered to show uncertainty or indifference.
examples: His shrug suggested that he did not know the answer.
She gave a small shrug and smiled.

senses.definition: To shake suddenly, often because of fear, disgust or cold.
examples: She shuddered at the thought of entering the dark room.
The old windows shuddered in the strong wind.

senses.definition: A sudden shaking movement caused by fear, disgust or cold.
examples: A shudder ran through him as the door creaked.
The building gave a slight shudder during the storm.

senses.definition: To breathe out audibly, often because of relief, sadness, tiredness or frustration.
examples: She sighed with relief when the test was over.
He sighed and closed the unfinished report.

senses.definition: A long, audible breath that expresses relief, sadness, tiredness or frustration.
examples: A sigh of relief came from the whole room.
He let out a deep sigh before answering.

senses.definition: To move down below a surface or to lower gradually; or to become weaker or less successful.
examples: The stone sank to the bottom of the lake.
The sun sank behind the mountains.

senses.definition: A fixed basin with a water supply and drain, used for washing dishes or hands.
examples: Please leave the dirty cups in the kitchen sink.
The bathroom sink needs a new tap.

senses.definition: To form a pleasant expression by turning up the corners of your mouth.
examples: She smiled when she saw her friends.
He smiled politely at the visitors.

senses.definition: A pleasant expression made by turning up the corners of the mouth.
examples: Her smile made the room feel warmer.
He greeted the child with a friendly smile.

senses.definition: To speak with repeated sounds or pauses, often because of nervousness or a speech difficulty.
examples: He began to stammer when the interviewer asked a difficult question.
She stammered an apology and looked down.

senses.definition: A way of speaking in which sounds or words are repeated or interrupted.
examples: His stammer became less noticeable when he felt relaxed.
The speech therapist helped him manage his stammer.
